subject: general
question: Ryotwari System of Revenue Collection was introduced in which part of British India?
solution:
Option **1** is correct, __**Southern India**__.

__
 
• **Ryotwari System (1820)-__**

 __
 
• It was prevalent in **Southern India**__.
 
• It was a major revenue collection method in British India which was majorly practiced in southern India, especially in Madras presidency.
 
• It was devised by **Captain Alexander Read** and **Thomas Munro**.
 
• Its principle was the direct collection of land revenue from each cultivator.
 
• This practice was beneficial as there was an elimination of middlemen in tax collection as collections were done by government agents.
 
 

 
• **Mahalwari System(1822):**

 
 
• It was Reintroduced with reform by **William Bentick**.
 
• It was introduced in central India especially Agra.
 
• In this, the whole land was divided into Mahals and the proprietors of Mahals were responsible for tax collection.
 
• It was a limited area reform, a temporary settlement.
 
 
 
• **Permanent System (1793):**
 
 
• It was introduced by **Lord Cornwallis**.
 
• Introduced in Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, and Varanasi.
 
• Zamindars, the owners of the land were given the right to collect the rent.
 
• The rent was divided into 11 parts out of which 1 part was iven to the Zamindar and rest to East India Company.
